Base directory for this skill: /private/tmp/tmp8nmqo5y4/pete/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/superpowers-dev/skills/test-driven-development

# Test-Driven Development (TDD)

## Overview

Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.

**Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.

**Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**

## When to Use

**Always:**
- New features
- Bug fixes
- Refactoring
- Behavior changes

**Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
- Throwaway prototypes
- Generated code
- Configuration files

Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.

## The Iron Law

```
NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
```

Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.

**No exceptions:**
- Don't keep it as "reference"
- Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
- Don't look at it
- Delete means delete

Implement fresh from tests. Period.

## Red-Green-Refactor

```dot
digraph tdd_cycle {
    rankdir=LR;
    red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
    verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
    green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccffcc"];
    verify_green [label="Verify passes\nAll green", shape=diamond];
    refactor [label="REFACTOR\nClean up", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccccff"];
    next [label="Next", shape=ellipse];

    red -> verify_red;
    verify_red -> green [label="yes"];
    verify_red -> red [label="wrong\nfailure"];
    green -> verify_green;
    verify_green -> refactor [label="yes"];
    verify_green -> green [label="no"];
    refactor -> verify_green [label="stay\ngreen"];
    verify_green -> next;
    next -> red;
}
```

### RED - Write Failing Test

Write one minimal test showing what should happen.

<Good>
```typescript
test('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {
  let attempts = 0;
  const operation = () => {
    attempts++;
    if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');
    return 'success';
  };

  const result = await retryOperation(operation);

  expect(result).toBe('success');
  expect(attempts).toBe(3);
});
```
Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
test('retry works', async () => {
  const mock = jest.fn()
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
  await retryOperation(mock);
  expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
});
```
Vague name, tests mock not code
</Bad>

**Requirements:**
- One behavior
- Clear name
- Real code (no mocks unless unavoidable)

### Verify RED - Watch It Fail

**MANDATORY. Never skip.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test fails (not errors)
- Failure message is expected
- Fails because feature missing (not typos)

**Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.

**Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.

### GREEN - Minimal Code

Write simplest code to pass the test.

<Good>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      if (i === 2) throw e;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('unreachable');
}
```
Just enough to pass
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(
  fn: () => Promise<T>,
  options?: {
    maxRetries?: number;
    backoff?: 'linear' | 'exponential';
    onRetry?: (attempt: number) => void;
  }
): Promise<T> {
  // YAGNI
}
```
Over-engineered
</Bad>

Don't add features, refactor other code, or "improve" beyond the test.

### Verify GREEN - Watch It Pass

**MANDATORY.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test passes
- Other tests still pass
- Output pristine (no errors, warnings)

**Test fails?** Fix code, not test.

**Other tests fail?** Fix now.

**"Other tests" means the project's suite, not just your file.** A
green run of the test you wrote is not a green suite. Before you call
the change done, run the project's test command (bare `pytest`,
`npm test`, `cargo test` — whatever the repo uses) even when your task
named only one test file. A scope statement in your task bounds the
deliverable, not your verification. Any failure that run shows —
including one you didn't cause — goes in your report by name; a red
test you watched scroll past and didn't mention is a report falsified
by omission.

### REFACTOR - Clean Up

After green only:
- Remove duplication
- Improve names
- Extract helpers

Keep tests green. Don't add behavior.

### Repeat

Next failing test for next feature.

## Good Tests

| Quality | Good | Bad |
|---------|------|-----|
| **Minimal** | One thing. "and" in name? Split it. | `test('validates email and domain and whitespace')` |
| **Clear** | Name describes behavior | `test('test1')` |
| **Shows intent** | Demonstrates desired API | Obscures what code should do |

When writing or changing any test, read [writing-good-tests.md](writing-good-tests.md) for the rules that keep tests honest:
- Name the production change that would make the test fail — before writing it
- Assert on real behavior, never on mock behavior
- Keep test-only code in test utilities, out of production classes
- Understand a dependency's side effects before mocking it

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Too simple to test" | Simple code breaks. Test takes 30 seconds. |
| "I'll test after" | Tests written after pass immediately — which proves nothing. They may test the wrong thing, test the implementation instead of the behavior, or miss the edge case you forgot. You never watched it fail, so you never proved it can catch the bug. Test-first forces that failure. |
| "Tests after achieve same goals (spirit not ritual)" | Tests-after answer "what does this do?"; tests-first answer "what should this do?" Tests written after are biased by the code you already wrote — you verify the cases you remembered, not the ones you'd have discovered. Coverage without proof the tests work. |
| "Already manually tested" | Manual testing is ad-hoc: no record of what you covered, no way to re-run it when the code changes, easy to forget cases under pressure. "Worked when I tried it" ≠ comprehensive. Automated tests run the same way every time. |
| "Deleting X hours is wasteful" | Sunk cost fallacy — that time is already spent either way. The real choice: rewrite with TDD (high confidence) vs. keep it and bolt tests on after (low confidence, likely bugs). Keeping code you can't trust is the waste. |
| "Keep as reference, write tests first" | You'll adapt it. That's testing after. Delete means delete. |
| "Need to explore first" | Fine. Throw away exploration, start with TDD. |
| "Test hard = design unclear" | Listen to test. Hard to test = hard to use. |
| "TDD will slow me down" | TDD IS the pragmatic path: catches bugs before commit, prevents regressions, lets you refactor without fear. "Pragmatic" shortcuts mean debugging in production — slower, not faster. |
| "Manual test faster" | Manual doesn't prove edge cases. You'll re-test every change. |
| "Existing code has no tests" | You're improving it. Add tests for existing code. |

## Red Flags - STOP and Start Over

- Code before test
- Test after implementation
- Test passes immediately
- Can't explain why test failed
- Tests added "later"
- Rationalizing "just this once"
- "I already manually tested it"
- "Tests after achieve the same purpose"
- "It's about spirit not ritual"
- "Keep as reference" or "adapt existing code"
- "Already spent X hours, deleting is wasteful"
- "TDD is dogmatic, I'm being pragmatic"
- "This is different because..."

**All of these mean: Delete code. Start over with TDD.**

## Example: Bug Fix

**Bug:** Empty email accepted

**RED**
```typescript
test('rejects empty email', async () => {
  const result = await submitForm({ email: '' });
  expect(result.error).toBe('Email required');
});
```

**Verify RED**
```bash
$ npm test
FAIL: expected 'Email required', got undefined
```

**GREEN**
```typescript
function submitForm(data: FormData) {
  if (!data.email?.trim()) {
    return { error: 'Email required' };
  }
  // ...
}
```

**Verify GREEN**
```bash
$ npm test
PASS
```

**REFACTOR**
Extract validation for multiple fields if needed.

## Verification Checklist

Before marking work complete:

- [ ] Every new function/method has a test
- [ ] Watched each test fail before implementing
- [ ] Each test failed for expected reason (feature missing, not typo)
- [ ] Wrote minimal code to pass each test
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
- [ ] Tests use real code (mocks only if unavoidable)
- [ ] Edge cases and errors covered

Can't check all boxes? You skipped TDD. Start over.

## When Stuck

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| Don't know how to test | Write wished-for API. Write assertion first. Ask your human partner. |
| Test too complicated | Design too complicated. Simplify interface. |
| Must mock everything | Code too coupled. Use dependency injection. |
| Test setup huge | Extract helpers. Still complex? Simplify design. |

## Debugging Integration

Bug found? Write failing test reproducing it. Follow TDD cycle. Test proves fix and prevents regression.

Never fix bugs without a test.

## Final Rule

```
Production code → test exists and failed first
Otherwise → not TDD
```

No exceptions without your human partner's permission.

import unittest
from decimal import Decimal

from kitty.errors import KittyError
from kitty.money import convert, fmt, parse_amount, parse_positive, split


class MoneyTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_parse_amount_accepts_plain_decimals(self):
        self.assertEqual(parse_amount("45"), Decimal("45.00"))
        self.assertEqual(parse_amount("45.5"), Decimal("45.50"))
        self.assertEqual(parse_amount("0.01"), Decimal("0.01"))

    def test_parse_amount_refuses(self):
        for bad in ["12.345", "0", "0.00", "-5", "abc", "", "1e2", "+5", ".5",
                    "5.", "NaN", "Infinity", " 5", "5\n"]:
            with self.assertRaises(KittyError, msg=bad):
                parse_amount(bad)

    def test_parse_positive(self):
        self.assertEqual(parse_positive("0.9234", "rate"), Decimal("0.9234"))
        for bad in ["0", "-1", "x", "1e3"]:
            with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
                parse_positive(bad, "rate")

    def test_fmt(self):
        self.assertEqual(fmt(Decimal("20.7")), "20.70")
        self.assertEqual(fmt(Decimal("-20.70")), "-20.70")
        self.assertEqual(fmt(Decimal("-0.00")), "0.00")

    def test_convert_rounds_half_up(self):
        self.assertEqual(convert(Decimal("45.00"), Decimal("0.92")), Decimal("41.40"))
        self.assertEqual(convert(Decimal("0.25"), Decimal("0.5")), Decimal("0.13"))
        self.assertEqual(convert(Decimal("1.00"), Decimal("0.125")), Decimal("0.13"))

    def test_split_equal_leftover_in_order(self):
        w = [("Alice", Decimal(1)), ("Bob", Decimal(1)), ("Cara", Decimal(1))]
        self.assertEqual(split(Decimal("10.00"), w),
                         {"Alice": Decimal("3.34"), "Bob": Decimal("3.33"), "Cara": Decimal("3.33")})
        w2 = [("Cara", Decimal(1)), ("Alice", Decimal(1)), ("Bob", Decimal(1))]
        self.assertEqual(list(split(Decimal("10.00"), w2).items())[0], ("Cara", Decimal("3.34")))

    def test_split_shares(self):
        self.assertEqual(split(Decimal("10.00"), [("A", Decimal(1)), ("B", Decimal(2))]),
                         {"A": Decimal("3.34"), "B": Decimal("6.66")})

    def test_split_two_leftover_cents(self):
        r = split(Decimal("0.05"), [("A", Decimal(1)), ("B", Decimal(1)), ("C", Decimal(1))])
        self.assertEqual(r, {"A": Decimal("0.02"), "B": Decimal("0.02"), "C": Decimal("0.01")})

    def test_split_percent_sums_to_total(self):
        r = split(Decimal("41.40"), [("A", Decimal(60)), ("B", Decimal(40))])
        self.assertEqual(r, {"A": Decimal("24.84"), "B": Decimal("16.56")})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
EOF

import os
import tempfile
import unittest

from kitty.errors import KittyError
from kitty.store import load, new_data, save


class StoreTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.path = os.path.join(self.tmp.name, "kitty.json")

    def tearDown(self):
        self.tmp.cleanup()

    def test_save_then_load_roundtrip(self):
        save(self.path, new_data("EUR"))
        self.assertEqual(load(self.path), new_data("EUR"))
        self.assertEqual(os.listdir(self.tmp.name), ["kitty.json"])

    def test_load_missing_file_raises(self):
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError) as cm:
            load(self.path)
        self.assertIn("init", str(cm.exception))

    def test_load_corrupt_json_raises(self):
        for content in ["{not json", "{}", "[]"]:
            with open(self.path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(content)
            with self.assertRaises(KittyError, msg=content):
                load(self.path)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
EOF

import unittest
from decimal import Decimal

from kitty.errors import KittyError
from kitty.ledger import Kitty
from kitty.store import new_data


class MembersTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.k = Kitty(new_data("EUR"))
        self.k.add_member("Alice")

    def test_add_and_list_in_join_order(self):
        self.k.add_member("Bob")
        self.assertEqual(self.k.members(), ["Alice", "Bob"])

    def test_add_trims_whitespace(self):
        self.k.add_member("  Bob ")
        self.assertEqual(self.k.members(), ["Alice", "Bob"])

    def test_add_duplicate_any_case_refused(self):
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            self.k.add_member("alice")

    def test_bad_names_refused(self):
        for bad in ["", "  ", "A,B", "A=B", "-x"]:
            with self.assertRaises(KittyError, msg=bad):
                self.k.add_member(bad)

    def test_find_member_case_insensitive(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.k.find_member("ALICE"), "Alice")
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            self.k.find_member("Zed")

    def test_remove_unused_member(self):
        self.k.add_member("Bob")
        self.k.remove_member("Bob")
        self.assertEqual(self.k.members(), ["Alice"])
        self.k.add_member("Bob")
        self.k.remove_member("bob")
        self.assertEqual(self.k.members(), ["Alice"])

    def test_remove_member_in_records_refused(self):
        self.k.add_member("Bob")
        self.k.add_member("Cara")
        self.k.data["expenses"] = [{"payer": "Alice", "shares": {"Alice": "1.00", "Bob": "1.00"}}]
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            self.k.remove_member("Bob")
        self.k.data["expenses"] = []
        self.k.data["payments"] = [{"from": "Cara", "to": "Alice"}]
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            self.k.remove_member("Alice")
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):

import unittest

from kitty.errors import KittyError
from kitty.ledger import Kitty
from kitty.store import new_data


def kitty_with(*names):
    k = Kitty(new_data("EUR"))
    for name in names:
        k.add_member(name)
    k.set_rate("USD", "0.92")
    return k


class BalancesTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.k = kitty_with("Alice", "Bob")
        self.k.add_expense("Alice", "45", "Dinner", among=["Alice", "Bob"], currency="USD",
                           date="2026-07-14", category="food")

    def test_spec_example_balances_and_settle(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.k.balances(), {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "-20.70"})
        self.assertEqual(self.k.settle(), [{"from": "Bob", "to": "Alice", "amount": "20.70"}])

    def test_payment_evens_out(self):
        self.k.add_payment("bob", "ALICE", "20.70")
        self.assertEqual(self.k.balances(), {"Alice": "0.00", "Bob": "0.00"})
        self.assertEqual(self.k.settle(), [])
        p = self.k.data["payments"][0]
        self.assertEqual((p["from"], p["to"], p["base_amount"]), ("Bob", "Alice", "20.70"))

    def test_payment_in_usd_converted_at_locked_rate(self):
        self.k.add_payment("Bob", "Alice", "10", currency="USD")
        self.k.set_rate("USD", "2")
        self.assertEqual(self.k.balances(), {"Alice": "11.50", "Bob": "-11.50"})

    def test_payment_refusals(self):
        for args, kw in [(("Bob", "bob", "5"), {}), (("Bob", "Zed", "5"), {}),
                         (("Bob", "Alice", "12.345"), {}), (("Bob", "Alice", "0"), {}),
                         (("Bob", "Alice", "5"), {"currency": "GBP"}),
                         (("Bob", "Alice", "5"), {"date": "2026-02-30"})]:
            with self.assertRaises(KittyError, msg=(args, kw)):
                self.k.add_payment(*args, **kw)
        self.assertEqual(self.k.data["payments"], [])

    def test_balances_include_zero_members(self):
        self.k.add_member("Cara")
        self.assertEqual(list(self.k.balances().items()),
                         [("Alice", "20.70"), ("Bob", "-20.70"), ("Cara", "0.00")])


class SettleTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_settle_ties_alphabetical_ignoring_case(self):
        k = kitty_with("Alice", "Cara", "bob", "Dan")
        k.add_expense("Alice", "30", "x", among=["Cara", "bob"])
        self.assertEqual(k.settle(), [{"from": "bob", "to": "Alice", "amount": "15.00"},
                                      {"from": "Cara", "to": "Alice", "amount": "15.00"}])

    def test_settle_tied_creditors_alphabetical(self):
        k = kitty_with("dan", "Bob", "Cara")
        k.add_expense("dan", "10", "x", among=["Cara"])
        k.add_expense("Bob", "10", "y", among=["Cara"])
        self.assertEqual(k.settle(), [{"from": "Cara", "to": "Bob", "amount": "10.00"},
                                      {"from": "Cara", "to": "dan", "amount": "10.00"}])

    def test_settle_largest_first(self):
        k = kitty_with("Alice", "Bob", "Cara", "Dan")
        k.add_expense("Alice", "60", "x", exact=[("Bob", "40"), ("Cara", "20")])
        k.add_expense("Dan", "30", "y", among=["Cara"])
        self.assertEqual(k.balances(), {"Alice": "60.00", "Bob": "-40.00", "Cara": "-50.00", "Dan": "30.00"})
        self.assertEqual(k.settle(), [{"from": "Cara", "to": "Alice", "amount": "50.00"},
                                      {"from": "Bob", "to": "Dan", "amount": "30.00"},
                                      {"from": "Bob", "to": "Alice", "amount": "10.00"}])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

    # Payments and balances

    def add_payment(self, sender: str, receiver: str, amount: str, *,
                    currency: Optional[str] = None, date: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
        sender = self.find_member(sender)
        receiver = self.find_member(receiver)
        if sender == receiver:
            raise KittyError("'%s' can't pay themselves" % sender)
        value = parse_amount(amount)
        currency = normalize_currency(currency) if currency is not None else self.data["base_currency"]
        rate = self.rate_for(currency)
        date = self.check_date(date)
        self.data["payments"].append({
            "seq": self._next_seq(),
            "date": date,
            "from": sender,
            "to": receiver,
            "amount": fmt(value),
            "currency": currency,
            "rate": str(rate),
            "base_amount": fmt(convert(value, rate)),
        })

    def balance_values(self) -> Dict[str, Decimal]:
        balances = {name: Decimal("0.00") for name in self.data["members"]}
        for e in self.data["expenses"]:
            balances[e["payer"]] += Decimal(e["base_amount"])
            for name, share in e["shares"].items():
                balances[name] -= Decimal(share)
        for p in self.data["payments"]:
            balances[p["from"]] += Decimal(p["base_amount"])
            balances[p["to"]] -= Decimal(p["base_amount"])
        return balances

    def balances(self) -> Dict[str, str]:
        return {name: fmt(value) for name, value in self.balance_values().items()}

    def settle(self) -> List[Dict[str, str]]:
        """While anyone isn't even, whoever owes most pays whoever is owed most,
        enough to even one of them out. Ties go alphabetically, ignoring case."""
        cents = {name: int(value * 100) for name, value in self.balance_values().items()}
        payments = []
        while any(cents.values()):
            debtor = min((n for n in cents if cents[n] < 0), key=lambda n: (cents[n], n.casefold()))
            creditor = min((n for n in cents if cents[n] > 0), key=lambda n: (-cents[n], n.casefold()))
            pay = min(-cents[debtor], cents[creditor])
            cents[debtor] += pay
            cents[creditor] -= pay
            payments.append({"from": debtor, "to": creditor, "amount": fmt(Decimal(pay) / 100)})
        return payments

import unittest

from kitty.errors import KittyError
from kitty.ledger import Kitty
from kitty.store import new_data

HEADER = ["id", "date", "payer", "description", "amount", "currency", "category", "base_amount"]


class ReportsTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.k = Kitty(new_data("EUR"))
        self.k.add_member("Alice")
        self.k.add_member("Bob")
        self.k.set_rate("USD", "0.92")
        self.k.add_expense("Alice", "45", "Dinner", among=["Alice", "Bob"], currency="USD",
                           date="2026-07-14", category="food")

    def test_spec_example_history(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.k.history("bob"), [
            {"date": "2026-07-14", "description": "Dinner", "change": "-20.70", "balance": "-20.70"}])

    def test_history_with_payment_and_order(self):
        self.k.add_payment("Bob", "Alice", "15.70", date="2026-07-15")
        self.k.add_expense("Bob", "10", "Taxi", among=["Alice", "Bob"], date="2026-07-13")
        self.assertEqual(self.k.history("Alice"), [
            {"date": "2026-07-13", "description": "Taxi", "change": "-5.00", "balance": "-5.00"},
            {"date": "2026-07-14", "description": "Dinner", "change": "20.70", "balance": "15.70"},
            {"date": "2026-07-15", "description": "Payment from Bob", "change": "-15.70", "balance": "0.00"},
        ])
        self.assertEqual(self.k.history("Bob")[-1],
                         {"date": "2026-07-15", "description": "Payment to Alice", "change": "15.70", "balance": "0.00"})

    def test_history_includes_zero_change_and_skips_unrelated(self):
        self.k.add_member("Cara")
        self.k.add_expense("Cara", "10", "Snack", among=["Cara"], date="2026-07-16")
        self.k.add_expense("Alice", "5", "Ice", among=["Bob"], date="2026-07-17")
        self.assertEqual(self.k.history("Cara"), [
            {"date": "2026-07-16", "description": "Snack", "change": "0.00", "balance": "0.00"}])

    def test_history_unknown_name_refused(self):
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            self.k.history("Zed")

    def test_spec_example_report(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.k.report(), {"food": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}})

    def test_report_sums_and_sorts(self):
        self.k.add_expense("Bob", "10", "Lunch", among=["Bob", "Alice"], category="food")
        self.k.add_expense("Alice", "30", "Kayak", among=["Bob"], category="activities")
        r = self.k.report()
        self.assertEqual(list(r), ["activities", "food"])
        self.assertEqual(r["activities"], {"Bob": "30.00"})
        self.assertEqual(list(r["food"].items()), [("Alice", "25.70"), ("Bob", "25.70")])

    def test_export_rows(self):
        rows = self.k.export_rows()
        self.assertEqual(rows[0], HEADER)
        self.assertEqual(rows[1], ["1", "2026-07-14", "Alice", "Dinner", "45.00", "USD", "food", "41.40"])

    def test_export_rows_keep_awkward_description(self):
        self.k.add_expense("Alice", "8", 'Café "Le Coin", Nice', date="2026-07-15")
        self.assertEqual(self.k.export_rows()[2][3], 'Café "Le Coin", Nice')


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

import csv
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

PROJECT_ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))


class CliTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.dir = self.tmp.name

    def tearDown(self):
        self.tmp.cleanup()

    def run_kitty(self, *args):
        env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONPATH=PROJECT_ROOT)
        result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "kitty"] + list(args), cwd=self.dir, env=env,
                                capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8")
        return result.returncode, result.stdout, result.stderr

    def ok(self, *args):
        code, out, err = self.run_kitty(*args)
        self.assertEqual((code, err), (0, ""), args)
        return out

    def kitty_bytes(self):
        with open(os.path.join(self.dir, "kitty.json"), "rb") as f:
            return f.read()

    def setup_dinner(self):
        self.ok("init", "EUR")
        self.ok("member", "add", "Alice")
        self.ok("member", "add", "Bob")
        self.ok("rate", "set", "USD", "0.92")
        return self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "45", "Dinner", "--currency", "USD",
                       "--date", "2026-07-14", "--category", "food")

    def test_spec_walkthrough(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.setup_dinner(), "1\n")
        expected = {
            ("member", "list"): '["Alice", "Bob"]',
            ("expense", "list"): '[{"id": 1, "date": "2026-07-14", "payer": "Alice", "description": "Dinner", '
                                 '"amount": "45.00", "currency": "USD", "base_amount": "41.40", "category": "food", '
                                 '"shares": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}]',
            ("balances",): '{"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "-20.70"}',
            ("settle",): '[{"from": "Bob", "to": "Alice", "amount": "20.70"}]',
            ("history", "Bob"): '[{"date": "2026-07-14", "description": "Dinner", "change": "-20.70", "balance": "-20.70"}]',
            ("report",): '{"food": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}',
        }
        for args, out in expected.items():
            self.assertEqual(self.ok(*args), out + "\n", args)

    def test_changing_commands_print_nothing(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("init", "eur"), "")
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("member", "add", "Alice"), "")
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(self.kitty_bytes())["base_currency"], "EUR")

    def test_description_words_and_option_anywhere(self):
        self.setup_dinner()
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "12", "Dinner", "--category", "food", "at", "the", "beach"), "2\n")
        e = json.loads(self.ok("expense", "list"))[1]
        self.assertEqual((e["description"], e["category"]), ("Dinner at the beach", "food"))

    def test_split_options_parse(self):
        self.setup_dinner()
        self.ok("member", "add", "Cara")
        self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "10", "a", "--among", "alice, Bob")
        self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "50", "b", "--exact", "Alice=30,bob=20")
        self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "10", "c", "--shares", "Alice=1,Bob=2")
        self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "45", "d", "--percent", "Alice=60,Bob=40", "--currency", "usd")
        shares = [e["shares"] for e in json.loads(self.ok("expense", "list"))[1:]]
        self.assertEqual(shares, [{"Alice": "5.00", "Bob": "5.00"}, {"Alice": "30.00", "Bob": "20.00"},
                                  {"Alice": "3.34", "Bob": "6.66"}, {"Alice": "24.84", "Bob": "16.56"}])

    def test_payment_and_remove_commands(self):
        self.setup_dinner()
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("payment", "add", "bob", "Alice", "20.70", "--date", "2026-07-15"), "")
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("balances"), '{"Alice": "0.00", "Bob": "0.00"}\n')
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("expense", "remove", "1"), "")
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("expense", "list"), "[]\n")
        self.ok("member", "add", "Cara")
        self.ok("member", "remove", "cara")
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("member", "list"), '["Alice", "Bob"]\n')

    def test_refusals_exit_1_stderr_file_unchanged(self):
        self.setup_dinner()
        before = self.kitty_bytes()
        bad_commands = [
            ["member", "add", "alice"], ["member", "remove", "Bob"], ["member", "add", "A,B"],
            ["member", "add"], ["member"], ["member", "rename", "x"],
            ["expense", "add", "Zed", "5", "x"], ["expense", "add", "Alice", "12.345", "x"],
            ["expense", "add", "Alice", "0", "x"], ["expense", "add", "Alice", "-5", "x"],
            ["expense", "add", "Alice", "abc", "x"], ["expense", "add", "Alice", "5", "x", "--currency", "GBP"],
            ["expense", "add", "Alice", "5", "x", "--percent", "Alice=50"],
            ["expense", "add", "Alice", "5", "x", "--exact", "Alice30"],
            ["expense", "add", "Alice", "5", "x", "--among", "Alice,"],
            ["expense", "add", "Alice", "5", "x", "--bogus", "1"],
            ["expense", "add", "Alice", "5", "x", "--date", "tomorrow"],
            ["expense", "add", "Alice", "5"], ["expense", "remove", "42"], ["expense", "remove"],
            ["payment", "add", "Bob", "bob", "5"], ["payment", "add", "Bob", "Alice", "1,5"],
            ["rate", "set", "EUR", "1"], ["rate", "set", "USD", "zero"],
            ["history", "Zed"], ["init", "EUR"], ["bogus"], [],
        ]
        for args in bad_commands:
            code, out, err = self.run_kitty(*args)
            self.assertEqual(code, 1, args)
            self.assertEqual(out, "", args)
            self.assertTrue(err.startswith("error: "), (args, err))
            self.assertNotIn("Traceback", err, args)
            self.assertEqual(self.kitty_bytes(), before, args)

    def test_no_kitty_file(self):
        code, out, err = self.run_kitty("balances")
        self.assertEqual(code, 1)
        self.assertIn("init", err)
        self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(os.path.join(self.dir, "kitty.json")))

    def test_corrupt_kitty_file(self):
        with open(os.path.join(self.dir, "kitty.json"), "w") as f:
            f.write("{oops")
        for args in [["balances"], ["member", "add", "Alice"]]:
            code, out, err = self.run_kitty(*args)
            self.assertEqual(code, 1)
            self.assertTrue(err.startswith("error: "))
            self.assertNotIn("Traceback", err)
            self.assertEqual(self.kitty_bytes(), b"{oops")

    def test_export_csv(self):
        self.setup_dinner()
        self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "8", 'Café "Le Coin", Nice', "--date", "2026-07-15")
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("export", "out.csv"), "")
        with open(os.path.join(self.dir, "out.csv"), newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            rows = list(csv.reader(f))
        self.assertEqual(rows[0], ["id", "date", "payer", "description", "amount", "currency", "category", "base_amount"])
        self.assertEqual(rows[1], ["1", "2026-07-14", "Alice", "Dinner", "45.00", "USD", "food", "41.40"])
        self.assertEqual(rows[2][3], 'Café "Le Coin", Nice')

    def test_export_unwritable_path(self):
        self.setup_dinner()
        before = self.kitty_bytes()
        code, out, err = self.run_kitty("export", "no/such/dir/out.csv")
        self.assertEqual(code, 1)
        self.assertTrue(err.startswith("error: "))
        self.assertNotIn("Traceback", err)
        self.assertEqual(self.kitty_bytes(), before)

    def test_unicode_name_output(self):
        self.ok("init", "EUR")
        self.ok("member", "add", "Zoë")
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("member", "list"), '["Zoë"]\n')


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

# Code Reviewer Prompt Template

Use this template when dispatching a code reviewer subagent.

**Purpose:** Review completed work against requirements and code quality standards before it cascades into more work.

```
Subagent (general-purpose):
  description: "Review code changes"
  prompt: |
    You are a Senior Code Reviewer with expertise in software architecture,
    design patterns, and best practices. Your job is to review completed work
    against its plan or requirements and identify issues before they cascade.

    ## What Was Implemented

    [DESCRIPTION]

    ## Requirements / Plan

    [PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS]

    ## Git Range to Review

    **Base:** [BASE_SHA]
    **Head:** [HEAD_SHA]

    ```bash
    git diff --stat [BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA]
    git diff [BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA]
    ```

    ## The spec is a vision document

    The spec says what the software must do. It does not enumerate every
    input, environment, or condition the software will meet. For behavior
    the spec is silent on, judge by what a reasonable person using this
    software would expect: a reasonable person's expectation is a
    requirement, and a spec's silence is not permission. Grade such
    findings by their effect on that person, not by whether the spec
    mentions the trigger.

    ## Declined to judge

    Before your verdict, list every behavior you considered and set aside
    as outside the plan or spec, one line each, with the reason. The
    executor rules on each line; nothing you set aside is dropped
    silently. An empty list means you set nothing aside.

    ## Read-Only Review

    Your review is read-only on this checkout. Do not mutate the working tree, the index, HEAD, or branch state in any way. Use tools like `git show`, `git diff`, and `git log` to inspect history. If you need a working copy of a different revision, check it out into a separate temporary directory (e.g. `git worktree add /tmp/review-[SHA] [SHA]`) — never move HEAD on this checkout.

    ## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents

    Do all of this review yourself. Never spawn a subagent to review part
    of the diff, and never spawn another reviewer for a second opinion.
    This process already provides every review seat the work gets; a
    reviewer you spawn duplicates one of them at full cost, and its
    verdict counts for nothing. If the diff feels too large for one
    pass, review it in passes yourself and say so in your report.

    ## What to Check

    **Plan alignment:**
    - Does the implementation match the plan / requirements?
    - Are deviations justified improvements, or problematic departures?
    - Is all planned functionality present?

    **Code quality:**
    - Clean separation of concerns?
    - Proper error handling?
    - Type safety where applicable?
    - DRY without premature abstraction?
    - Edge cases handled?

    **Architecture:**
    - Sound design decisions?
    - Reasonable scalability and performance?
    - Security concerns?
    - Integrates cleanly with surrounding code?

    **Testing:**
    - Tests verify real behavior, not mocks?
    - Edge cases covered?
    - Integration tests where they matter?
    - All tests passing?

    **Production readiness:**
    - Migration strategy if schema changed?
    - Backward compatibility considered?
    - Documentation complete?
    - No obvious bugs?

    ## Calibration

    Categorize issues by actual severity. Not everything is Critical.
    Acknowledge what was done well before listing issues — accurate praise
    helps the implementer trust the rest of the feedback.

    If you find significant deviations from the plan, flag them specifically
    so the implementer can confirm whether the deviation was intentional.
    If you find issues with the plan itself rather than the implementation,
    say so.

    ## Output Format

    ### Strengths
    [What's well done? Be specific.]

    ### Issues

    #### Critical (Must Fix)
    [Bugs, security issues, data loss risks, broken functionality]

    #### Important (Should Fix)
    [Architecture problems, missing features, poor error handling, test gaps]

    #### Minor (Nice to Have)
    [Code style, optimization opportunities, documentation polish]

    For each issue:
    - File:line reference
    - What's wrong
    - Why it matters
    - How to fix (if not obvious)

    ### Recommendations
    [Improvements for code quality, architecture, or process]

    ### Assessment

    **Ready to merge?** [Yes | No | With fixes]

    **Reasoning:** [1-2 sentence technical assessment]

    ## Critical Rules

    **DO:**
    - Categorize by actual severity
    - Be specific (file:line, not vague)
    - Explain WHY each issue matters
    - Acknowledge strengths
    - Give a clear verdict

    **DON'T:**
    - Say "looks good" without checking
    - Mark nitpicks as Critical
    - Give feedback on code you didn't actually read
    - Be vague ("improve error handling")
    - Avoid giving a clear verdict
```

**Placeholders:**
- `[DESCRIPTION]` — brief summary of what was built
- `[PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS]` — what it should do (plan file path, task text, or requirements)
- `[BASE_SHA]` — starting commit
- `[HEAD_SHA]` — ending commit

**Reviewer returns:** Strengths, Issues (Critical / Important / Minor), Recommendations, Assessment

## Example Output

```
### Strengths
- Clean database schema with proper migrations (db.ts:15-42)
- Comprehensive test coverage (18 tests, all edge cases)
- Good error handling with fallbacks (summarizer.ts:85-92)

### Issues

#### Important
1. **Missing help text in CLI wrapper**
   - File: index-conversations:1-31
   - Issue: No --help flag, users won't discover --concurrency
   - Fix: Add --help case with usage examples

2. **Date validation missing**
   - File: search.ts:25-27
   - Issue: Invalid dates silently return no results
   - Fix: Validate ISO format, throw error with example

#### Minor
1. **Progress indicators**
   - File: indexer.ts:130
   - Issue: No "X of Y" counter for long operations
   - Impact: Users don't know how long to wait

### Recommendations
- Add progress reporting for user experience
- Consider config file for excluded projects (portability)

### Assessment

**Ready to merge: With fixes**

**Reasoning:** Core implementation is solid with good architecture and tests. Important issues (help text, date validation) are easily fixed and don't affect core functionality.
```

1	# Kitty: shared trip costs — design
2	
3	## Intent
4	
5	A small command-line tool for tracking shared costs on trips with friends, so
6	that at the end everyone knows who owes whom. The owner is not a programmer;
7	their friend Sam will drive it from scripts and a spreadsheet, so every report
8	prints machine-readable JSON and expenses export to CSV.
9	
10	## Goals
11	
12	- Record expenses (with flexible splits and foreign currencies) and repayments.
13	- Show balances, a settle-up plan, per-person history, a category report, and
14	  a CSV export.
15	- Money is always exact: no floating point, shares always sum exactly to the
16	  expense total.
17	- Clear error messages and exit status 1 on any bad input — never a traceback.
18	
19	## Non-goals
20	
21	- No GUI, no network, no live exchange rates, no multi-file/multi-trip
22	  management (one `kitty.json` per folder).
23	- No editing of expenses (remove and re-add instead), no removing payments.
24	
25	## Anti-goals
26	
27	- Old expenses changing value when a rate is later changed.
28	- Silently rounding bad input (e.g. `12.345`) instead of refusing it.
29	- Silently losing history (e.g. by removing a member who appears in records).
30	
31	## Constraints
32	
33	- Runs with the macOS system Python (**3.9.6**) and the standard library only.
34	  No `match`, no `X | Y` type syntax at runtime, no third-party packages.
35	- Invoked as `python3 -m kitty <command> ...` from the folder containing the
36	  `kitty/` package. Data lives in `kitty.json` in the **current working
37	  directory**.
38	
39	## Approaches considered
40	
41	1. **Small package with separate modules + stdlib `unittest` tests** — chosen.
42	   Money math, storage, commands, and CLI parsing each in their own module;
43	   easy for Sam to read and extend; tests pin down the cent-distribution rules.
44	2. **Single `kitty.py` file** — same invocation, fewer files, but everything
45	   tangled; harder to extend. Rejected.
46	3. **Store raw inputs only, recompute everything each run** — conflicts with
47	   rate locking (old expenses would be re-valued). Rejected; each expense
48	   stores its rate, converted amount, and computed shares at creation time.
49	
50	The owner left the build approach to the builder; option 1 is the builder's
51	call.
52	
53	## Decided behaviour (by the owner)
54	
55	### Commands
56	
57	- `init CUR` — create a new kitty with base currency `CUR`.
58	- `member add NAME`, `member remove NAME`, `member list`.
59	- `expense add PAYER AMOUNT DESCRIPTION...` — prints the new expense's ID.
60	  Options: `--among A,B` | `--exact A=30,B=20` | `--shares A=2,B=1` |
61	  `--percent A=60,B=40` (at most one of these), `--currency CUR`,
62	  `--date YYYY-MM-DD` (default today), `--category NAME` (default `other`).
63	- `expense list`, `expense remove ID`.
64	- `payment add FROM TO AMOUNT` with `--currency`, `--date`.
65	- `rate set CUR VALUE` — 1 CUR = VALUE base currency.
66	- `balances`, `settle`, `history NAME`, `report`, `export FILE`.
67	
68	### Output formats (JSON, money as strings with two decimals)
69	
70	- `member list`: `["Alice", "Bob"]`
71	- `expense list`: `[{"id": 1, "date": "2026-07-14", "payer": "Alice",
72	  "description": "Dinner", "amount": "45.00", "currency": "USD",
73	  "base_amount": "41.40", "category": "food",
74	  "shares": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}]`
75	- `balances`: `{"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "-20.70"}`
76	- `settle`: `[{"from": "Bob", "to": "Alice", "amount": "20.70"}]`
77	- `history Bob`: `[{"date": "2026-07-14", "description": "Dinner",
78	  "change": "-20.70", "balance": "-20.70"}]`
79	- `report`: `{"food": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}`
80	- Money is in the base currency, except an expense's own `amount`.
81	- `export FILE`: CSV with columns `id, date, payer, description, amount,
82	  currency, category, base_amount`.
83	
84	### Errors
85	
86	Any invalid input (unknown member, non-number amount, etc.) prints a message
87	saying what is wrong **on stderr**, exits with status 1, and leaves
88	`kitty.json` **exactly as it was** (byte for byte; validate everything before
89	saving anything). No tracebacks.
90	
91	### Amounts
92	
93	- Must be a positive number with at most two decimals. `12.345`, `0`, `-5`,
94	  `abc` are all **refused**, never rounded.
95	
96	### Currencies and rates
97	
98	- `rate set` for the base currency is refused.
99	- An expense/payment in a non-base currency with no rate set is refused, with
100	  a message saying no rate is set and how to set one.
101	- The rate in effect when an entry is added is **locked** into that entry:
102	  its `base_amount` is computed and stored then. Changing the rate later only
103	  affects new entries.
104	- Conversion: `base_amount = amount × rate`, rounded to the cent, **halves
105	  up** (0.125 → 0.13).
106	
107	### Splitting
108	
109	- Default: equally among everyone who is a member **at the time the expense
110	  is added**.
111	- Every share is first its exact amount **rounded down** to the cent; the
112	  leftover cents are then handed out **one each, in order**: the order typed
113	  in `--among`/`--shares`/`--percent`/`--exact`, or the order people joined
114	  the group when split among everyone.
115	  - €10 among Alice, Bob, Cara → 3.34, 3.33, 3.33.
116	  - 10.00 with `--shares A=1,B=2` → A 3.34, B 6.66.
117	- `--exact` amounts are in the expense's own currency and must add up exactly
118	  to the expense amount; `--percent` values must add up to 100. Otherwise
119	  refused.
120	- Shares are stored in the base currency and always add up exactly to
121	  `base_amount`.
122	
123	### Settling
124	
125	While anyone is not even: the person who owes the most pays the person who is
126	owed the most, the smaller of the two amounts (evening out at least one of
127	them). Ties are broken alphabetically, ignoring case. Payments are listed in
128	the order they are produced.
129	
130	### Names
131	
132	- Case-insensitive: `alice` and `Alice` are the same person. Adding `alice`
133	  when `Alice` exists is refused. Any spelling works in any command.
134	- Always displayed as first added.
135	- Names may not contain `,` or `=`.
136	
137	### Removing members
138	
139	Refused if the person appears in any expense or payment (as payer, sharer,
140	sender or receiver). Otherwise allowed.
141	
142	## Builder's calls (owner agreed to these as proposals or left them open)
143	
144	- **Foreign-currency splits:** convert the total first (halves up), then split
145	  `base_amount` with the round-down-and-hand-out rule. For `--exact` in a
146	  foreign currency, the weights are the exact amounts, so each base share is
147	  `base_amount × exact_i / amount` rounded down, leftovers in listed order.
148	  (In the base currency this reproduces the exact amounts.)
149	- **One splitting algorithm:** every split is "weights → exact proportional
150	  part of the base total in cents → floor → leftover cents one each in list
151	  order". Equal = weight 1 each; shares = the given numbers; percent = the
152	  given percentages; exact = the given amounts. Leftover is always fewer
153	  cents than there are people.
154	- **Weights validation:** `--shares` and `--percent` values must be positive
155	  numbers (decimals allowed). `--exact` values follow the amount rules
156	  (positive, ≤ 2 decimals). Names in any list must be members, may not repeat,
157	  and the list may not be empty. Only one of the four split options at a time.
158	- Rates must be positive numbers; any number of decimals allowed; stored as a
159	  string. Setting a rate again replaces it.
160	- Payment to oneself is refused. Payer of an expense need not be among the
161	  sharers.
162	- Expense IDs start at 1, increase, and are never reused after removal.
163	- `balances` lists all current members in join order, including `0.00`.
164	  `balance = paid base_amounts − own shares + payments sent − payments
165	  received`. (Paying someone back raises your balance and lowers theirs.)
166	- Ordering: `expense list`, `history`, and `export` sort by date, then by
167	  the order entries were typed. Expenses and payments share one internal
168	  sequence counter so they interleave correctly in `history`.
169	- `history NAME`: one row per expense they paid or shared in (`change` =
170	  paid − share, description = the expense's) and per payment they sent
171	  (`+amount`, description `Payment to X`) or received (`−amount`, description
172	  `Payment from X`); `balance` is the running total. Exact zero-change
173	  expense rows are still listed.
174	- `report`: categories sorted alphabetically; within each, only people with
175	  a share in that category, in join order. Category stored as typed.
176	- Currency codes: case-insensitive, stored uppercase, must be three letters.
177	- Dates must be valid `YYYY-MM-DD`; default is today's local date.
178	- `init` refuses if `kitty.json` already exists. Every other command refuses
179	  with a clear message if it doesn't.
180	- Successful changing commands print nothing, except `expense add`, which
181	  prints the ID (just the number). `export` overwrites FILE if it exists.
182	- JSON printed compact on one line in the examples' style
183	  (`json.dumps` default separators), with `ensure_ascii=False` so accented
184	  names print as typed.
185	- Description is all remaining words joined with spaces; options may appear
186	  anywhere after the command.
187	- `kitty.json` written atomically (temp file + rename) so a crash can't leave
188	  it half-written. Stores amounts and rates as decimal strings.
189	- Errors go to stderr prefixed `error: `; usage mistakes (unknown command,
190	  missing argument) also exit 1.
191	
192	- Amount syntax: plain decimals only (`45`, `45.5`, `45.50`); refuse
193	  exponents (`1e2`), signs (`+5`), and leading/trailing dots (`.5`, `5.`).
194	  The same syntax applies to rates, shares and percents (any decimals for
195	  those).
196	- `report` includes everyone listed as a sharer, even when their share
197	  rounded to `0.00`.
198	- CSV export includes a header row.
199	- Names: surrounding whitespace is trimmed; empty names and names starting
200	  with `-` are refused; inner spaces are allowed (quote them in the shell).
201	
202	## Left to the builder
203	
204	Module layout, internal names, the exact wording of error messages, and the
205	test structure.

1	"""Money parsing, formatting, conversion and splitting (all Decimal, no floats)."""
     2	
     3	import re
     4	from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal
     5	from typing import Dict, List, Tuple
     6	
     7	from kitty.errors import KittyError
     8	
     9	CENT = Decimal("0.01")
    10	_NUMBER = re.compile(r"[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?")
    11	
    12	
    13	def _parse_plain(text: str) -> Decimal:
    14	    if not isinstance(text, str) or not _NUMBER.fullmatch(text):
    15	        raise ValueError(text)
    16	    return Decimal(text)
    17	
    18	
    19	def parse_amount(text: str) -> Decimal:
    20	    """A positive amount with at most two decimals; never rounded."""
    21	    message = "amount must be a positive number with at most two decimals, got %r" % text
    22	    try:
    23	        value = _parse_plain(text)
    24	    except ValueError:
    25	        raise KittyError(message)
    26	    if value <= 0 or value.as_tuple().exponent < -2:
    27	        raise KittyError(message)
    28	    return value.quantize(CENT)
    29	
    30	
    31	def parse_positive(text: str, what: str) -> Decimal:
    32	    """A positive number with any number of decimals (rates, shares, percents)."""
    33	    message = "%s must be a positive number, got %r" % (what, text)
    34	    try:
    35	        value = _parse_plain(text)
    36	    except ValueError:
    37	        raise KittyError(message)
    38	    if value <= 0:
    39	        raise KittyError(message)
    40	    return value
    41	
    42	
    43	def fmt(value: Decimal) -> str:
    44	    value = Decimal(value).quantize(CENT)
    45	    if value == 0:
    46	        value = abs(value)
    47	    return "{:.2f}".format(value)
    48	
    49	
    50	def convert(amount: Decimal, rate: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    51	    return (amount * rate).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
    52	
    53	
    54	def split(total: Decimal, weights: List[Tuple[str, Decimal]]) -> Dict[str, Decimal]:
    55	    """Split total by weights: each part rounded down to the cent, then the
    56	    leftover cents go one each to the names in the order given."""
    57	    cents = int(total * 100)
    58	    weight_sum = sum(w for _, w in weights)
    59	    parts = [(name, int((cents * w) // weight_sum)) for name, w in weights]
    60	    left = cents - sum(p for _, p in parts)
    61	    return {
    62	        name: (Decimal(p + (1 if i < left else 0)) / 100).quantize(CENT)
    63	        for i, (name, p) in enumerate(parts)
    64	    }
     1	"""Loading and saving kitty.json."""
     2	
     3	import json
     4	import os
     5	import tempfile
     6	
     7	from kitty.errors import KittyError
     8	
     9	FILE_NAME = "kitty.json"
    10	_KEYS = ("version", "base_currency", "members", "rates", "next_id", "next_seq", "expenses", "payments")
    11	
    12	
    13	def new_data(base_currency: str) -> dict:
    14	    return {
    15	        "version": 1,
    16	        "base_currency": base_currency,
    17	        "members": [],
    18	        "rates": {},
    19	        "next_id": 1,
    20	        "next_seq": 1,
    21	        "expenses": [],
    22	        "payments": [],
    23	    }
    24	
    25	
    26	def load(path: str) -> dict:
    27	    if not os.path.exists(path):
    28	        raise KittyError("no kitty here; run 'python3 -m kitty init CUR' first")
    29	    try:
    30	        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
    31	            data = json.load(f)
    32	    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:

1	"""The kitty itself: members, rates, expenses and payments, and the reports
     2	built from them. Every refusal raises KittyError."""
     3	
     4	import datetime
     5	import re
     6	from decimal import Decimal
     7	from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
     8	
     9	from kitty.errors import KittyError
    10	from kitty.money import convert, fmt, parse_amount, parse_positive, split
    11	
    12	
    13	def normalize_currency(text: str) -> str:
    14	    if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z]{3}", text):
    15	        raise KittyError("currency must be a three-letter code like EUR, got %r" % text)
    16	    return text.upper()
    17	
    18	
    19	class Kitty:
    20	    def __init__(self, data: dict):
    21	        self.data = data
    22	
    23	    # Members
    24	
    25	    def members(self) -> List[str]:
    26	        return list(self.data["members"])
    27	
    28	    def find_member(self, name: str) -> str:
    29	        wanted = name.strip().casefold()
    30	        for member in self.data["members"]:
    31	            if member.casefold() == wanted:
    32	                return member
    33	        raise KittyError("'%s' is not in the group" % name)
    34	
    35	    def add_member(self, name: str) -> None:
    36	        name = name.strip()
    37	        if not name:
    38	            raise KittyError("a name can't be empty")
    39	        if name.startswith("-"):
    40	            raise KittyError("a name can't start with '-', got %r" % name)
    41	        if "," in name or "=" in name:
    42	            raise KittyError("a name can't contain ',' or '=', got %r" % name)
    43	        for member in self.data["members"]:
    44	            if member.casefold() == name.casefold():
    45	                raise KittyError("'%s' is already in the group" % member)
    46	        self.data["members"].append(name)
    47	
    48	    def remove_member(self, name: str) -> None:
    49	        member = self.find_member(name)
    50	        in_expense = any(
    51	            e["payer"] == member or member in e["shares"] for e in self.data["expenses"]
    52	        )
    53	        in_payment = any(member in (p["from"], p["to"]) for p in self.data["payments"])
    54	        if in_expense or in_payment:
    55	            raise KittyError("can't remove '%s': they appear in an expense or payment" % member)
    56	        self.data["members"].remove(member)
    57	
    58	    # Rates
    59	
    60	    def set_rate(self, currency: str, value: str) -> None:
    61	        currency = normalize_currency(currency)
    62	        if currency == self.data["base_currency"]:
    63	            raise KittyError("%s is the main currency; rates are only for other currencies" % currency)
    64	        rate = parse_positive(value, "rate")
    65	        self.data["rates"][currency] = str(rate)
    66	
    67	    def rate_for(self, currency: str) -> Decimal:
    68	        currency = normalize_currency(currency)
    69	        if currency == self.data["base_currency"]:
    70	            return Decimal(1)
    71	        if currency not in self.data["rates"]:
    72	            raise KittyError("no rate set for %s; use 'rate set %s VALUE' first" % (currency, currency))
    73	        return Decimal(self.data["rates"][currency])
    74	
    75	    # Expenses
    76	
    77	    @staticmethod
    78	    def check_date(text: Optional[str]) -> str:
    79	        if text is None:
    80	            return datetime.date.today().isoformat()
    81	        try:
    82	            if not re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", text):
    83	                raise ValueError(text)
    84	            datetime.date.fromisoformat(text)
    85	        except ValueError:
    86	            raise KittyError("date must be a real date written YYYY-MM-DD, got %r" % text)
    87	        return text
    88	
    89	    def _resolve_names(self, names: List[str]) -> List[str]:
    90	        if not names:
    91	            raise KittyError("the list of people to split between is empty")
    92	        resolved = [self.find_member(name) for name in names]
    93	        if len(set(resolved)) != len(resolved):
    94	            raise KittyError("someone is listed more than once in the split")
    95	        return resolved
    96	
    97	    def _weights(self, amount: Decimal, among, exact, shares, percent) -> List[Tuple[str, Decimal]]:
    98	        chosen = [opt for opt in (among, exact, shares, percent) if opt is not None]
    99	        if len(chosen) > 1:
   100	            raise KittyError("use only one of --among, --exact, --shares and --percent")
   101	        if among is not None:
   102	            return [(name, Decimal(1)) for name in self._resolve_names(among)]
   103	        if exact is not None:
   104	            names = self._resolve_names([name for name, _ in exact])
   105	            values = [parse_amount(value) for _, value in exact]
   106	            if sum(values) != amount:
   107	                raise KittyError("the --exact amounts add up to %s, not %s" % (fmt(sum(values)), fmt(amount)))
   108	            return list(zip(names, values))
   109	        if shares is not None:
   110	            names = self._resolve_names([name for name, _ in shares])
   111	            return list(zip(names, [parse_positive(value, "a share") for _, value in shares]))
   112	        if percent is not None:
   113	            names = self._resolve_names([name for name, _ in percent])
   114	            values = [parse_positive(value, "a percentage") for _, value in percent]
   115	            if sum(values) != 100:
   116	                raise KittyError("the --percent values add up to %s, not 100" % sum(values))
   117	            return list(zip(names, values))
   118	        if not self.data["members"]:
   119	            raise KittyError("the group is empty; add people with 'member add NAME' first")
   120	        return [(name, Decimal(1)) for name in self.data["members"]]
   121	
   122	    def _next_seq(self) -> int:
   123	        seq = self.data["next_seq"]
   124	        self.data["next_seq"] = seq + 1
   125	        return seq
   126	
   127	    def add_expense(self, payer: str, amount: str, description: str, *,
   128	                    among: Optional[List[str]] = None,
   129	                    exact: Optional[List[Tuple[str, str]]] = None,
   130	                    shares: Optional[List[Tuple[str, str]]] = None,
   131	                    percent: Optional[List[Tuple[str, str]]] = None,
   132	                    currency: Optional[str] = None,
   133	                    date: Optional[str] = None,
   134	                    category: Optional[str] = None) -> int:
   135	        payer = self.find_member(payer)
   136	        value = parse_amount(amount)
   137	        currency = normalize_currency(currency) if currency is not None else self.data["base_currency"]
   138	        rate = self.rate_for(currency)
   139	        date = self.check_date(date)
   140	        weights = self._weights(value, among, exact, shares, percent)
   141	        base_amount = convert(value, rate)
   142	        expense_id = self.data["next_id"]
   143	        self.data["next_id"] = expense_id + 1
   144	        self.data["expenses"].append({
   145	            "id": expense_id,
   146	            "seq": self._next_seq(),
   147	            "date": date,
   148	            "payer": payer,
   149	            "description": description,
   150	            "amount": fmt(value),
   151	            "currency": currency,
   152	            "rate": str(rate),
   153	            "base_amount": fmt(base_amount),
   154	            "category": category if category is not None else "other",
   155	            "shares": {name: fmt(share) for name, share in split(base_amount, weights).items()},
   156	        })
   157	        return expense_id
   158	
   159	    def remove_expense(self, expense_id: str) -> None:
   160	        for expense in self.data["expenses"]:
   161	            if str(expense["id"]) == expense_id:
   162	                self.data["expenses"].remove(expense)
   163	                return
   164	        raise KittyError("there is no expense with ID %r" % expense_id)
   165	
   166	    def _sorted(self, entries: List[dict]) -> List[dict]:
   167	        return sorted(entries, key=lambda e: (e["date"], e["seq"]))
   168	
   169	    def list_expenses(self) -> List[dict]:
   170	        keys = ("id", "date", "payer", "description", "amount", "currency", "base_amount", "category")
   171	        result = []
   172	        for e in self._sorted(self.data["expenses"]):
   173	            row = {key: e[key] for key in keys}
   174	            row["shares"] = dict(e["shares"])
   175	            result.append(row)
   176	        return result
   177	
   178	    # Payments and balances
   179	
   180	    def add_payment(self, sender: str, receiver: str, amount: str, *,
   181	                    currency: Optional[str] = None, date: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
   182	        sender = self.find_member(sender)
   183	        receiver = self.find_member(receiver)
   184	        if sender == receiver:
   185	            raise KittyError("'%s' can't pay themselves" % sender)
   186	        value = parse_amount(amount)
   187	        currency = normalize_currency(currency) if currency is not None else self.data["base_currency"]
   188	        rate = self.rate_for(currency)
   189	        date = self.check_date(date)
   190	        self.data["payments"].append({
   191	            "seq": self._next_seq(),
   192	            "date": date,
   193	            "from": sender,
   194	            "to": receiver,
   195	            "amount": fmt(value),
   196	            "currency": currency,
   197	            "rate": str(rate),
   198	            "base_amount": fmt(convert(value, rate)),
   199	        })
   200	
   201	    def balance_values(self) -> Dict[str, Decimal]:
   202	        balances = {name: Decimal("0.00") for name in self.data["members"]}
   203	        for e in self.data["expenses"]:
   204	            balances[e["payer"]] += Decimal(e["base_amount"])
   205	            for name, share in e["shares"].items():
   206	                balances[name] -= Decimal(share)
   207	        for p in self.data["payments"]:
   208	            balances[p["from"]] += Decimal(p["base_amount"])
   209	            balances[p["to"]] -= Decimal(p["base_amount"])
   210	        return balances
   211	
   212	    def balances(self) -> Dict[str, str]:
   213	        return {name: fmt(value) for name, value in self.balance_values().items()}
   214	
   215	    def settle(self) -> List[Dict[str, str]]:
   216	        """While anyone isn't even, whoever owes most pays whoever is owed most,
   217	        enough to even one of them out. Ties go alphabetically, ignoring case."""
   218	        cents = {name: int(value * 100) for name, value in self.balance_values().items()}
   219	        payments = []
   220	        while any(cents.values()):
   221	            debtor = min((n for n in cents if cents[n] < 0), key=lambda n: (cents[n], n.casefold()))
   222	            creditor = min((n for n in cents if cents[n] > 0), key=lambda n: (-cents[n], n.casefold()))
   223	            pay = min(-cents[debtor], cents[creditor])
   224	            cents[debtor] += pay
   225	            cents[creditor] -= pay
   226	            payments.append({"from": debtor, "to": creditor, "amount": fmt(Decimal(pay) / 100)})
   227	        return payments
   228	
   229	    # Reports
   230	
   231	    def history(self, name: str) -> List[Dict[str, str]]:
   232	        member = self.find_member(name)
   233	        entries = []
   234	        for e in self.data["expenses"]:
   235	            if e["payer"] == member or member in e["shares"]:
   236	                paid = Decimal(e["base_amount"]) if e["payer"] == member else Decimal(0)
   237	                change = paid - Decimal(e["shares"].get(member, "0"))
   238	                entries.append((e, e["description"], change))
   239	        for p in self.data["payments"]:
   240	            if p["from"] == member:
   241	                entries.append((p, "Payment to %s" % p["to"], Decimal(p["base_amount"])))
   242	            elif p["to"] == member:
   243	                entries.append((p, "Payment from %s" % p["from"], -Decimal(p["base_amount"])))
   244	        entries.sort(key=lambda item: (item[0]["date"], item[0]["seq"]))
   245	        rows = []
   246	        balance = Decimal(0)
   247	        for entry, description, change in entries:
   248	            balance += change
   249	            rows.append({"date": entry["date"], "description": description,
   250	                         "change": fmt(change), "balance": fmt(balance)})
   251	        return rows
   252	
   253	    def report(self) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, str]]:
   254	        totals = {}  # type: Dict[str, Dict[str, Decimal]]
   255	        for e in self.data["expenses"]:
   256	            category = totals.setdefault(e["category"], {})
   257	            for name, share in e["shares"].items():
   258	                category[name] = category.get(name, Decimal(0)) + Decimal(share)
   259	        order = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(self.data["members"])}
   260	        return {
   261	            category: {name: fmt(totals[category][name])
   262	                       for name in sorted(totals[category], key=lambda n: order.get(n, len(order)))}
   263	            for category in sorted(totals)
   264	        }
   265	
   266	    def export_rows(self) -> List[List[str]]:
   267	        rows = [["id", "date", "payer", "description", "amount", "currency", "category", "base_amount"]]
   268	        for e in self.list_expenses():
   269	            rows.append([str(e["id"]), e["date"], e["payer"], e["description"], e["amount"],
   270	                         e["currency"], e["category"], e["base_amount"]])
   271	        return rows

1	"""Command-line entry point: python3 -m kitty COMMAND ..."""
     2	
     3	import argparse
     4	import csv
     5	import json
     6	import os
     7	import sys
     8	from typing import List, Optional, Tuple
     9	
    10	from kitty import store
    11	from kitty.errors import KittyError
    12	from kitty.ledger import Kitty, normalize_currency
    13	
    14	COMMANDS = ("init CUR, member add|remove|list, expense add|list|remove, payment add, "
    15	            "rate set, balances, settle, history NAME, report, export FILE")
    16	GROUPS = ("member", "expense", "payment", "rate")
    17	
    18	
    19	class _Parser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    20	    """An ArgumentParser that reports mistakes as KittyError (exit status 1)."""
    21	
    22	    def __init__(self, prog: str):
    23	        super().__init__(prog="python3 -m kitty " + prog, add_help=False, allow_abbrev=False)
    24	
    25	    def error(self, message):
    26	        raise KittyError("%s: %s" % (self.prog.replace("python3 -m kitty ", ""), message))
    27	
    28	
    29	def _names(text: str) -> List[str]:
    30	    names = [part.strip() for part in text.split(",")]
    31	    if any(not name for name in names):
    32	        raise KittyError("empty name in list %r" % text)
    33	    return names
    34	
    35	
    36	def _pairs(text: str) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
    37	    pairs = []
    38	    for part in text.split(","):
    39	        name, sep, value = part.partition("=")
    40	        if not sep or not name.strip() or not value.strip():
    41	            raise KittyError("expected NAME=VALUE pairs separated by commas, got %r" % text)
    42	        pairs.append((name.strip(), value.strip()))
    43	    return pairs
    44	
    45	
    46	def _parse(prog: str, args: List[str], *positionals, options=(), rest: Optional[str] = None):
    47	    parser = _Parser(prog)
    48	    for name in positionals:
    49	        parser.add_argument(name)
    50	    if rest:
    51	        parser.add_argument(rest, nargs="+")
    52	    for option in options:
    53	        parser.add_argument("--" + option)
    54	    return parser.parse_intermixed_args(args)
    55	
    56	
    57	def _json(value) -> str:
    58	    return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False)
    59	
    60	
    61	def _export(kitty: Kitty, path: str) -> None:
    62	    try:
    63	        with open(path, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    64	            csv.writer(f).writerows(kitty.export_rows())
    65	    except OSError as e:
    66	        raise KittyError("cannot write %s: %s" % (path, e.strerror))
    67	
    68	
    69	def run(argv: List[str]) -> None:
    70	    if not argv:
    71	        raise KittyError("no command given; commands are: " + COMMANDS)
    72	    command = argv[0]
    73	    if command in GROUPS:
    74	        if len(argv) < 2:
    75	            raise KittyError("'%s' needs a subcommand; commands are: %s" % (command, COMMANDS))
    76	        command = argv[0] + " " + argv[1]
    77	        args = argv[2:]
    78	    else:
    79	        args = argv[1:]
    80	
    81	    path = store.FILE_NAME
    82	    if command == "init":
    83	        a = _parse("init", args, "currency")
    84	        currency = normalize_currency(a.currency)
    85	        if os.path.exists(path):
    86	            raise KittyError("%s already exists here; not overwriting it" % path)
    87	        store.save(path, store.new_data(currency))
    88	        return
    89	
    90	    handlers = {
    91	        "member add": _member_add, "member remove": _member_remove, "member list": _member_list,
    92	        "expense add": _expense_add, "expense list": _expense_list, "expense remove": _expense_remove,
    93	        "payment add": _payment_add, "rate set": _rate_set,
    94	        "balances": _balances, "settle": _settle, "history": _history, "report": _report,
    95	        "export": _export_cmd,
    96	    }
    97	    if command not in handlers:
    98	        raise KittyError("unknown command %r; commands are: %s" % (command, COMMANDS))
    99	    kitty = Kitty(store.load(path))
   100	    changed, output = handlers[command](kitty, args)
   101	    if changed:
   102	        store.save(path, kitty.data)
   103	    if output is not None:
   104	        print(output)
   105	
   106	
   107	# Each handler returns (changed, output): whether the kitty must be saved, and
   108	# the text to print once it has been.
   109	
   110	def _member_add(kitty, args):
   111	    kitty.add_member(_parse("member add", args, "name").name)
   112	    return True, None
   113	
   114	
   115	def _member_remove(kitty, args):
   116	    kitty.remove_member(_parse("member remove", args, "name").name)
   117	    return True, None
   118	
   119	
   120	def _member_list(kitty, args):
   121	    _parse("member list", args)
   122	    return False, _json(kitty.members())
   123	
   124	
   125	def _expense_add(kitty, args):
   126	    a = _parse("expense add", args, "payer", "amount", rest="description",
   127	               options=("among", "exact", "shares", "percent", "currency", "date", "category"))
   128	    expense_id = kitty.add_expense(
   129	        a.payer, a.amount, " ".join(a.description),
   130	        among=_names(a.among) if a.among is not None else None,
   131	        exact=_pairs(a.exact) if a.exact is not None else None,
   132	        shares=_pairs(a.shares) if a.shares is not None else None,
   133	        percent=_pairs(a.percent) if a.percent is not None else None,
   134	        currency=a.currency, date=a.date, category=a.category)
   135	    return True, str(expense_id)
   136	
   137	
   138	def _expense_list(kitty, args):
   139	    _parse("expense list", args)
   140	    return False, _json(kitty.list_expenses())
   141	
   142	
   143	def _expense_remove(kitty, args):
   144	    kitty.remove_expense(_parse("expense remove", args, "id").id)
   145	    return True, None
   146	
   147	
   148	def _payment_add(kitty, args):
   149	    a = _parse("payment add", args, "sender", "receiver", "amount", options=("currency", "date"))
   150	    kitty.add_payment(a.sender, a.receiver, a.amount, currency=a.currency, date=a.date)
   151	    return True, None
   152	
   153	
   154	def _rate_set(kitty, args):
   155	    a = _parse("rate set", args, "currency", "value")
   156	    kitty.set_rate(a.currency, a.value)
   157	    return True, None
   158	
   159	
   160	def _balances(kitty, args):
   161	    _parse("balances", args)
   162	    return False, _json(kitty.balances())
   163	
   164	
   165	def _settle(kitty, args):
   166	    _parse("settle", args)
   167	    return False, _json(kitty.settle())
   168	
   169	
   170	def _history(kitty, args):
   171	    return False, _json(kitty.history(_parse("history", args, "name").name))
   172	
   173	
   174	def _report(kitty, args):
   175	    _parse("report", args)
   176	    return False, _json(kitty.report())
   177	
   178	
   179	def _export_cmd(kitty, args):
   180	    _export(kitty, _parse("export", args, "file").file)
   181	    return False, None
   182	
   183	
   184	def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
   185	    try:
   186	        run(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
   187	    except KittyError as e:
   188	        print("error: %s" % e, file=sys.stderr)
   189	        return 1
   190	    return 0
